title: Cascade Harness Radar — Score & Capability Contract (v1)
description: The canonical shape for NUMERIC evidence (score_snapshot), the six-axis HARNESS capability taxonomy and synthesized capability_vector, numbers-vs-discourse divergence_flag entries, and the per-run source_health_report. Sibling of Model Radar's score-schema.json — slugs, source_ref, and the three-level categorical confidence scale ('low' | 'medium' | 'high', NEVER 0..1 numeric) are shared conventions. THE KEY DIFFERENCE FROM MODEL RADAR: the subject of a harness score is the HARNESS (harness_slug), not a raw model. A harness benchmark result is almost always a harness+model COMBO (e.g. 'openhands' running 'claude-fable-5' scoring 68.4% resolved on SWE-bench Verified), so score_snapshot keys on harness_slug (required) and carries model_slug as OPTIONAL context (which underlying model produced the number). PERSISTENCE CONVENTION — score snapshots accumulate APPEND-ONLY in dossier package type_data.score_snapshots (on both harness and benchmark dossiers) and on evidence package type_data.score_snapshots; the latest capability_vector persists STRUCTURED at the harness-dossier package's type_data.capability_vector, separate from the prose artifact body. DEDUPE RULE — a snapshot whose {source_slug, benchmark_slug, harness_slug, model_slug, metric, as_of} tuple is identical to an existing entry is SKIPPED; prior entries are never overwritten or deleted (a researcher's lab notebook, not a mutable cache). SCORING RUBRIC — axis values are integers 0-100 RELATIVE TO THE CURRENT FRONTIER of harnesses at synthesis time: 90-100 frontier-leading, 70-89 strong/competitive, 40-69 mid-pack, <40 weak/unproven. Confidence: 'high' = corroborated across stances or from a rigorous independent eval; 'medium' = single credible source or partially corroborated; 'low' = anecdotal, contested, or maker-only with no independent check.

slug.description: Lowercase-hyphenated canonical slug: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, with dots permitted inside version tokens. Examples — harnesses: 'openhands', 'aider', 'claude-code', 'codex-cli', 'swe-agent', 'cline'; benchmarks: 'swe-bench-verified', 'terminal-bench', 'aider-polyglot'; models (optional context): 'claude-fable-5', 'gpt-5'.

confidence.description: Categorical confidence — the ONE confidence scale for this contract, shared with dossier-schema.json. 'high' = corroborated across stances or from a rigorous independent eval; 'medium' = single credible source or partially corroborated; 'low' = anecdotal, contested, or maker-only with no independent check.

source_ref.description: Attribution for one piece of evidence backing a claim — SAME shape as dossier-schema.json source_ref. url should be the normalized canonical URL (dedup-comparable, matching the /cse:ingest convention: lowercased host, utm_*/fbclid/gclid + fragment + trailing slash stripped).

url.description: Normalized canonical URL of the source.

author.description: Person or outlet behind the source (e.g. 'All Hands AI', 'Aider', 'SWE-bench team', 'Terminal-Bench').

source_id.description: Optional id of the registry entry in sources.json this evidence was harvested from.

stance.description: Stance of THIS evidence item — may override the source's default stance_hint. Same enum as dossier-schema.json.

published_date.description: ISO date the source was published, if discoverable.

core_axis_id.description: The SIX core HARNESS capability axes — fixed taxonomy, order matters (this enum order is the canonical display order). These rate the HARNESS/agent scaffold, NOT the underlying model. 1) 'agentic_capability' (label 'Agentic Capability') — autonomous multi-step task completion on real coding work: plan/act/observe loops, multi-file edits, test-and-repair; fed by SWE-bench Verified / Terminal-Bench / Aider polyglot resolved-rates ACHIEVED WITH THIS HARNESS. 2) 'context_management' (label 'Context Management') — repo-scale context handling: repo maps, code search/retrieval, context compaction, and memory across long horizons. 3) 'tool_integration' (label 'Tools & Extensibility') — breadth and quality of tool use and extensibility: MCP support, shell/browser/editor tools, hooks, subagents, custom tools and plugins. 4) 'model_flexibility' (label 'Model Flexibility') — model-agnosticism and provider breadth: BYO-model, multi-provider, local models, or locked to one vendor. 5) 'control_safety' (label 'Control & Safety') — permissioning, sandboxing/isolation, human-in-the-loop approval, diff review, and guardrails against destructive actions. 6) 'ecosystem_maturity' (label 'Ecosystem & Maturity') — adoption, documentation, release cadence/stability, surface coverage (CLI / IDE / cloud), and community/support. NOTE: cost/token efficiency is intentionally NOT a core axis (it is dominated by the chosen model, not the harness) — score it as an emergent axis ('token_efficiency') only when Aider-style per-task cost data or throughput data is available.

score_snapshot.title: Score Snapshot
score_snapshot.description: ONE observed number for ONE harness (optionally a harness+model combo) from ONE leaderboard/eval source on ONE date — the atomic unit of numeric evidence. Snapshots accumulate append-only (see top-level persistence convention); the dedupe key is the {source_slug, benchmark_slug, harness_slug, model_slug, metric, as_of} tuple. Snapshots record what a source SAID on a date, not what is true — synthesis weighs them by source stance and rigor. Harness benchmark results are harness-sensitive by definition, so recording the underlying model (model_slug) and scaffold config (config) is load-bearing, not optional decoration.

benchmark_slug.description: Canonical benchmark slug the number belongs to (e.g. 'swe-bench-verified', 'terminal-bench', 'aider-polyglot'). Matches dossier-schema.json benchmark_dossier identity slugs.

harness_slug.description: Canonical harness/agent slug the number was measured for (e.g. 'openhands', 'aider', 'swe-agent', 'claude-code'). This is the PRIMARY subject of a harness score. Matches dossier-schema.json harness_dossier identity slugs.

model_slug.description: OPTIONAL canonical model slug the harness ran to produce this number (e.g. 'claude-fable-5', 'gpt-5'). Harness scores are almost always harness+model combos — record the underlying model whenever the source discloses it, since the same harness swings widely across models.

metric.description: What kind of number this is (e.g. 'resolved_rate', 'accuracy', 'pass_at_1', 'tasks_completed', 'usd_per_task'). Lowercase snake_case; keep metric names consistent per benchmark so time series line up.

value.description: The observed numeric value, in the units declared by 'unit' (e.g. 68.4 with unit 'percent', 2.31 with unit 'usd').

unit.description: Unit of 'value' (e.g. 'percent', 'usd', 'tasks'). Keep unit strings consistent per metric so snapshots are comparable over time.

as_of.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) the number was OBSERVED on the source (the harvest/observation date, not a release date). Part of the dedupe key — the same number observed on a later date is a NEW snapshot (that's the time series).

source_url.description: Normalized URL of the page the number was read from (same normalization convention as source_ref.url).

source_slug.description: id of the sources.json 'leaderboards' registry entry this snapshot was harvested from (e.g. 'swe-bench', 'terminal-bench', 'aider-polyglot'). Part of the dedupe key.

notes.description: Optional free-text caveat or context for this specific number (e.g. 'Verified split only', 'best of 3 attempts', 'self-reported').

config.description: Optional scaffold/config caveat for the HARNESS run (e.g. 'CodeAct v3', 'bash-only', 'diff edit format', 'with test-time compute'). Harness leaderboard numbers are scaffold-sensitive — record the config whenever the source discloses it. (Analogous to Model Radar's 'harness' field, inverted: here the harness is the subject and this records its internal configuration.)

evidence_package_id.description: Optional Cascade evidence package id this snapshot was extracted from, when the number arrived via the evidence pipeline rather than a direct leaderboard harvest.

axis_score.title: Axis Score
axis_score.description: One synthesized HARNESS capability rating on one axis. value is an integer 0-100 RELATIVE TO THE CURRENT FRONTIER of harnesses at synthesis time: 90-100 frontier-leading, 70-89 strong/competitive, 40-69 mid-pack, <40 weak/unproven. The rationale MUST cite specific evidence — a score snapshot (benchmark + number) or an evidence package — never a vibe. When numeric evidence is thin (common for closed harnesses that don't publish benchmark configs), score anyway but set confidence 'low' and say so in the rationale.

axis.description: Axis id: one of the six core_axis_id values ('agentic_capability', 'context_management', 'tool_integration', 'model_flexibility', 'control_safety', 'ecosystem_maturity') OR an emergent axis slug (e.g. 'token_efficiency', 'multimodal', 'cloud_autonomy').

label.description: Optional human-readable display label (e.g. 'Tools & Extensibility' for axis 'tool_integration').

value.description: Integer 0-100, relative to the current frontier of harnesses at synthesis time (see scoring rubric in the axis_score description).

rationale.description: REQUIRED evidence citation: which score snapshots (benchmark + number + date) and/or evidence packages support this value. A rationale that cites no specific evidence is invalid by convention.

sources.description: Optional source attributions backing the rationale — same source_ref shape as dossier-schema.json.

emergent_axis_score.title: Emergent Axis Score
emergent_axis_score.description: An axis_score PLUS a required definition, for capability dimensions the six core axes don't cover. EMERGENT-AXIS RULES — emergent axes are OPTIONAL and added only when 2+ INDEPENDENT evidence items support a capability dimension outside the core taxonomy (e.g. 'token_efficiency' when Aider-style per-task cost data exists, 'multimodal' for screenshot/vision-driven agents, 'cloud_autonomy' for fully-unattended cloud agents); ids are slug-form; an emergent axis must NEVER duplicate a core axis; each carries its own definition so future synthesis runs score it consistently.

axis.description: Emergent axis slug (e.g. 'token_efficiency', 'multimodal'). Must not be one of the six core_axis_id values.

value.description: Integer 0-100, relative to the current frontier at synthesis time (same rubric as axis_score).

rationale.description: REQUIRED evidence citation, same rule as axis_score — and for an emergent axis the cited evidence must include the 2+ independent items that justify the axis existing at all.

definition.description: REQUIRED: what this emergent axis measures and why the evidence supports adding it beyond the six core axes.

sources.description: Optional source attributions backing the rationale.

capability_vector.title: Capability Vector
capability_vector.description: The synthesized capability rating for ONE harness at ONE moment. At synthesis time ALL SIX core axes are REQUIRED (score thin axes honestly at low confidence rather than omitting them); emergent axes are optional and rule-gated (see emergent_axis_score). The LATEST capability_vector persists structured at the harness-dossier package's type_data.capability_vector, separate from the prose artifact body — prose renders FROM this structure, never the other way around.

harness_slug.description: Canonical harness slug this vector rates (e.g. 'openhands'). Optional here because the vector usually lives ON the harness-dossier package whose identity already carries the slug; include it whenever the vector travels alone.

core.description: ALL SIX core axes, each exactly once, in core_axis_id enum order: agentic_capability, context_management, tool_integration, model_flexibility, control_safety, ecosystem_maturity. A vector missing a core axis is invalid — when evidence is thin, score the axis at low confidence and note it in insufficient_evidence.

emergent.description: Optional emergent axes beyond the core six — each requires 2+ independent evidence items and its own definition (see emergent_axis_score rules). Never duplicate a core axis.

synthesized_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the synthesis run that produced this vector. Required — scores are frontier-relative, so they are meaningless without their synthesis time.

insufficient_evidence.description: Optional honest statement when one or more axes rest on thin evidence (e.g. 'control_safety scored from docs alone; no independent red-team of the permission model available'). Prefer saying this plainly over inflating confidence.

divergence_flag.title: Divergence Flag
divergence_flag.description: A flagged mismatch between what the NUMBERS say and what the DISCOURSE says — e.g. a harness tops SWE-bench Verified while practitioners report it thrashes on large real repos, or a maker claims full autonomy while independent runs need heavy babysitting. This is the numbers-vs-narrative complement to dossier-schema.json's divergence_entry (source-vs-source disagreement). Preserving the mismatch, rather than averaging it away, is the point.

topic.description: What the divergence is about (e.g. 'real-repo reliability vs. SWE-bench Verified score').

numbers_say.description: REQUIRED: what the structured score snapshots show, with the specific numbers (e.g. 'OpenHands+CodeAct v3 68.4% resolved on SWE-bench Verified as of 2026-04, near the top of the board').

discourse_says.description: REQUIRED: what maker claims and/or practitioner discourse say that diverges from the numbers (e.g. 'practitioners report frequent loop-stalls and high token burn on repos larger than the benchmark tasks').

axis.description: Optional core axis id ('agentic_capability', 'context_management', 'tool_integration', 'model_flexibility', 'control_safety', 'ecosystem_maturity') when the divergence maps cleanly onto one — it should then temper that axis's confidence in the capability_vector.

assessment.description: Optional researcher judgment: which side the evidence favors and why, or 'unresolved'.

sources.description: Optional source attributions for both sides of the divergence.

source_health_report.title: Source Health Report
source_health_report.description: Per-run health record for a leaderboard harvest. BEST-EFFORT RUNG SEMANTICS — every enabled leaderboard source is attempted independently; a failed source NEVER aborts the run. Each failure is recorded here with its error instead of raised, so the run degrades gracefully and the researcher can see exactly which rungs held and which slipped.

run_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the harvest run this report describes.

sources.description: One entry per attempted leaderboard source (every enabled sources.json 'leaderboards' entry the run touched).

source_slug.description: id of the sources.json 'leaderboards' entry that was attempted.

status.description: 'fetched' = page retrieved but no numbers extracted yet/at all; 'parsed' = numbers successfully extracted into snapshots; 'failed' = fetch or parse errored (see 'error'). A 'failed' source never aborts the run.

snapshot_count.description: How many score snapshots this source yielded this run (0 for fetched-but-unparsed or failed sources).

error.description: Optional error message when status is 'failed' (or a warning worth keeping for a degraded parse).

url.description: Optional URL actually fetched (useful when a fallback like r.jina.ai was used instead of the registry url).
